[ 3 ] Although never confirmed, Marie Laurencin believed that she had Creole heritage through her maternal grandmother, something she saw as part of her identity her whole life. [ 4 ] Her father, fiscal administrator Alfred-Stanislas Toulet (1839–1905), visited her during her childhood and paid for her education. [ 3 ] At 18, she studied porcelain painting in Sèvres . She then returned to Paris and continued her art education at the Académie Humbert, where she changed her focus to oil painting . Marie Laurencin, 1909, Réunion à la campagne ( Apollinaire et ses amis ), oil on canvas, 130 x 194 cm, Musée Picasso , Paris. Reproduced in The Cubist Painters, Aesthetic Meditations (1913) During the early years of the 20th century, Laurencin was an important figure in the Parisian avant-garde . A member of both the circle of Pablo Picasso , and Cubists associated with the Section d'Or , such as Jean Metzinger , Albert Gleizes , Robert Delaunay , Henri le Fauconnier , and Francis Picabia , exhibiting with them at the Salon des Indépendants (1910–1911) and the Salon d'Automne (1911–1912), and Galeries Dalmau (1912) at the first Cubist exhibition in Spain. She became romantically involved with the poet Guillaume Apollinaire , and has often been identified as his muse. In addition, Laurencin had important connections to the salon of the American expatriate and lesbian writer Natalie Clifford Barney . She had relationships with men and women, [ 5 ] and her art reflected her life, her "balletic wraiths" and "sidesaddle Amazons " providing the art world with her brand of "queer femme with a Gallic twist." [ 6 ] She had a forty years long love relationship with fashion designer Nicole Groult [ fr ] . During the First World War , Laurencin left France for exile in Spain with her German-born husband, the artist, Baron Otto von Waëtjen, since through her marriage she had automatically lost her French citizenship. The couple subsequently lived together briefly in Düsseldorf . She was greatly affected by her separation from the French capital, the unrivaled center of artistic creativity. [ 7 ] After they divorced in 1920, she returned to Paris, where she achieved financial success as an artist until the economic depression of the 1930s. During the 1930s she worked as an art instructor at a private school. She lived in Paris until her death.

168781749227.title: 1879 Hand Painted chromolithograph By John Gerrard Keulemans Crested Eagles
168781749227.desc: The selected region displays an antique ornithological print of "Morphnus taeniatus", which is the historical scientific name given to the dark-morph variant of the Crested Eagle (Morphnus guianensis). Print Details • Publication: This hand-colored lithograph was published in 1879 within the prestigious ornithological journal The Ibis (Series 4, Volume 3, Plate III). • Artist: The illustration was created by the renowned Dutch bird artist John Gerrard Keulemans (J.G. Keulemans lith.) and printed by Hanhart. • Historical Context: When British ornithologist John Gerrard Gurney first described this specimen from Sarayacu, Ecuador in 1879, he classified it as a distinct species (Morphnus taeniatus) due to its striking, heavily barred dark plumage. Modern taxonomy eventually recognized that this was simply a dark color morph of the Crested Eagle rather than a separate species. • Provenance: The top of the page features a letterhead from Florian J. Shasky Rare Books and Manuscripts, a well-known dealer formerly based in Palo Alto, California.

920015042881.title: SUPER RARE Vintage RICH RUDISH SIGNED ARTIST PROFF,  "The Troika," Equine Art
920015042881.desc: This rare vintage Rich Rudish print titled "The Troika" is a signed, personal dedication, artist proof, making it a highly sought-after collectible item. Created in 1986 in California, this original lithography artwork features Arabian Stallions as its subject, showcasing Rudish's distinctive illustration style. To bring such iconic horses to life, Breyer approached artist Rich Rudish with the idea. Rich, a California native, was an artisan with many different talents, including illustration, sculpture, and even animation. He had been working with Hallmark as a product line designer since the 1960s, and one of his best-known projects was their “Rainbow Brite” franchise. Rainbow Brite’s horse, Starlite, was a product entirely of Rich’s own – his distinct Arabian style is Rich’s calling card. In addition to the animation special “Rainbow Brite and the Star Stealer,” Rich also worked on another 1980s cartoon favorite, “The Real Ghostbusters.” (His son Paul Rudish carries on that legacy today, working on animation projects including “My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic,” “Star Wars: The Clone Wars,” and “Mickey Mouse." The piece showcases his masterful command of equine anatomy and movement, adapting a classic subject through his signature highly stylized, dramatic lens. True to Rudish’s background as both a commercial illustrator for Hallmark and a fine artist, his depiction of The Troika features fiercely dynamic, high-stepping horses with prominent "dishfaced profiles," hyper-expressive eyes, and sweeping, elegant manes. Measuring 20 inches in length and 18 inches in height, this medium-sized print is a valuable addition to any art collection, especially for fans of Rudish, original signed equine art, and contemporary art from the 1980s. 860027577471.title: Vintage W.S. George Radisson H.K. China 22K Gold Courting Couple Teacup Saucer
860027577471.desc: Beautiful Vintage American 22-Karat Gold Courting Couple China Offered is a beautiful vintage teacup and saucer featuring a romantic Courting Couple / Colonial Couple scene surrounded by elegant 22-karat gold filigree decoration. This distinctive set represents a wonderful collaboration between two American pottery and decorating companies and is a great example of the ornate, romantic china popular in the 1930s–1950s. Manufacturer & History The saucer carries the faint green underglaze marking: “Radisson — W.S. George — Made in USA” The W.S. George Pottery Company, based in East Palestine, Ohio, produced the porcelain blank using its popular Radisson scalloped shape. The pieces were then decorated by H.K. China, an independent decorating company associated with the Sebring, Ohio pottery district. H.K. China purchased undecorated white blanks from manufacturers such as W.S. George and added the elaborate gold decoration and romantic transfer designs. The overglaze gold marking reads: “Warranted H.K. China, 22 Karat” This indicates the use of genuine 22-karat gold decoration, adding both historical and collector appeal. Design The centerpiece features a charming romantic courting couple, sometimes described by collectors as a Fragonard-style or Colonial Couple scene. The figures are surrounded by ornate gold scrollwork and filigree, complemented by the elegant scalloped Radisson form. The combination of the romantic transfer, heavy gold decoration, and American-made porcelain gives this piece a wonderful Old-World / Americana appearance. Approximate Era 1930s–1950s This type of heavily decorated gold china was particularly popular during this period and was produced for the American market. Condition Excellent vintage condition. Please examine all photographs carefully, as the pictures are considered part of the description. 800766216023.title: Original Iwao Nakajima Oil Painting Casa De Frutas 1977, Signed.
800766216023.desc: Iwao Nakajima (1934–2011) was a prominent Japanese-Brazilian painter best known for his work in the *naïf* (naive art) style. He was born in Gunma Prefecture, Japan, where he began his studies at the Nagoya Ceramics and Porcelain Research Institute. In the 1950s, he emigrated to Brazil to work as a specialist technician in enamel and porcelain painting. Over the years, he became a naturalized Brazilian citizen and settled permanently in Embu das Artes, in the state of São Paulo—a town renowned as a hub for local artists. Key aspects of his life and work include: Artistic Style: His work established itself within the *naïf* art genre. He was poetically described as "a poet who writes with a paintbrush" due to the lyricism, harmony, and subtle color blending with which he depicted nature, pastoral landscapes, and everyday Brazilian scenes (such as his famous paintings of the historic town of Paraty). Career: He was an active member of the *Associação Paulista de Belas Artes* (São Paulo Fine Arts Association). His paintings were featured in numerous solo and group exhibitions, shown not only in Brazil and Japan but also in international cities such as New York and Milan. Legacy: Today, his works are held in both public and private collections, including that of the São Paulo Parliament Art Museum (*Museu de Arte do Parlamento de São Paulo*). In recognition of his cultural impact, a viaduct in the city of Embu das Artes officially bears his name.

One side reveals an elegant multi-tiered pagoda nestled dramatically among rugged cliffs, while the opposite side depicts travelers journeying through a peaceful mountain pass beneath weathered pines. Delicate washes of ink-like gray, soft earth tones, and carefully placed accents of blue and green create remarkable depth throughout the composition. Encircling the artwork are richly decorated cobalt blue borders highlighted with intricate raised gold scrollwork, floral ornament, and geometric motifs. 407279447517.desc: Antique Boye Needle Company Rotary Store Counter Dispenser Cabinet **Circa 1910s–1920s | Authentic Industrial General Store Country Mercantile Hardware** Up for auction is a remarkable, fully intact vintage Boye Needle Company circular rotary countertop mercantile dispenser. Invented by James H. Boye, these unique rotating "Commodity Cabinets" completely revolutionized early 20th-century retail logistics by providing general store clerks with an all-in-one spinning cross-reference station. The top dial mechanism serves as a master index wheel where spinning the selector needle pointer to a particular machine manufacturer instantly points out which interchangeable bobbins, shuttles, or needle packets a home dressmaker required. This is a phenomenal, highly sought-after centerpiece item for antique advertising collectors, sewing enthusiasts, and industrial farmhouse decor spaces! ### Product Details & Structural Features: * **Brand / Manufacturer:** The Boye Needle Co. (Chicago, Illinois) * **Item:** Complete Rotary Countertop Needle & Bobbin Dispenser Unit * **Era:** Early 20th Century (Patented 1906, 1907 - Circa 1910-1925) * **Visual Graphics:** Features bold red and black master lettering reading: *"Boye Needles, Shuttles and Bobbins For Your Machine."* * **Historical Labels:** Retains fragments of the rare, original paper perimeter cross-reference chart displaying classic consumer brands like *Elgin Rotary*, *Free Rotary*, *Free-Westinghouse*, *General Electric*, *New Home*, and *Gray Bar*. * **Interior Carousel:** The bottom view displays the intricate radial layout designed to cleanly drop individual wooden inventory tubes or accessory bobbins into categorized slots. ### Condition Notes: This cabinet is in authentic, wonderfully weathered antique condition with incredible character. * **Metal Dial Face:** Shows stunning natural age-related patina, surface oxidation spots, light storage scuffs, and superficial scratches from real-world mercantile counter use. All alphabetical text remains legible. The original pointer hardware handles operate cleanly. * **Paper Charts:** The side wrap labels display historic character wear, complete with localized staining, discoloration, and small edge tears, but many of the vintage sewing machine line names remain beautifully intact and readable.

800777284231.desc: Item Description: For sale is an authentic matching set of 5 antique Japanese porcelain miniature sauce dishes (Mame-zara / 豆皿), dating to the late Meiji or Taisho era (late 19th century to 1920s). Each miniature dish features an intricate, hand-painted central motif of an auspicious, legendary Asian Phoenix (Hō-ō) soaring amidst vibrant overglaze iron-red flames and stylized blue cloud clusters. The perimeter of each dish is beautifully framed with a continuous, layered scale or feather geometric border executed in a deep jade/teal-green enamel palette. Due to their diminutive size, these traditional Mame-zara are incredibly versatile. While historically used for single servings of strong condiments, side garnishes, or dipping sauces, they make highly sought-after contemporary display accents, vanity ring dishes, or coin catchalls. Base Marking: The underside of each dish features an overglaze red double-bordered square studio seal reading 「若林製」 (Wakabayashi Sei / Made by Wakabayashi). This specific maker mark guarantees authentic, historic Japanese kiln heritage. Dimensions: Diameter: Miniature Size (Under 4 inches) Condition Details: This antique set is in good overall condition, showing excellent structural integrity with no major hairline cracks or large structural breaks. Due to their handmade, hand-decorated nature from the late Meiji or Taisho era, there are minor artisanal variations across the plates. Specifically, as shown in the close-up images, one plate features a small area of light enamel loss/glaze skips on a blue cloud motif and isolated, tiny black kiln-iron spots embedded in the glaze from the original historical firing process. These features are highly typical of authentic period porcelain and add to its historic character. Light shelf wear is present on the unglazed base rings. Please inspect the high-resolution close-ups to confirm exact cosmetic condition.

227560319161.title: Vintage West African Iron Cuff
227560319161.desc: A lovely antique currency bracelet from the Akan tribes that are divided between westAfrica's Ivory Coast and Ghana. The Akan consist of several different tribes, all of which are proficient in metal casting, typically using the lost wax method.This bronze (copper alloy) bracelet is a fine example of Akan craftsmanship andwas probably made by the Baule people of the Ivory Coast. 147637343700.title: c1910 Hamilton Grade 926 18s 17J Gold Filled Pocket Watch Runs Intermittently
147637343700.desc: Offered here is a handsome early Hamilton pocket watch dating to approximately 1910, built around Hamilton's substantial Grade 926, 18-size, 17-jewel movement and housed in a marked gold-filled open-face case. This is not simply an unidentified antique pocket watch with a Hamilton dial. The movement is clearly signed and identifiable as Hamilton's Grade 926, one of the company's large early full-plate movements, and the watch retains a very traditional early American presentation with a white signed dial, oversized black Arabic numerals, red five-minute markings, subsidiary seconds and blue-toned hands. The watch does run, but operation is intermittent. It should be purchased with the expectation that it will require professional service or repair. Dating the Watch The movement serial visible in the photographs appears to read approximately: 809608 Published Hamilton serial-number tables place this serial range around 1910 , making a circa 1910 date highly consistent with the movement. As with many early American watches, serial-number chronology should be treated as an approximate manufacturing date rather than an exact day of completion. A date of approximately 1910 places this watch firmly within the great early twentieth-century period of American pocket-watch production. Hamilton Watch Company Hamilton Watch Company was established in Lancaster, Pennsylvania during the 1890s and became one of the major American watch manufacturers of the twentieth century. Hamilton earned its reputation through high-quality American-made movements, particularly precision pocket watches, and eventually became closely associated with railroad timekeeping. The present watch is fitted with Hamilton's Grade 926 , an early large-format movement that predates many of the smaller Hamilton movements collectors encounter more frequently today. The Grade 926 was produced over a long period beginning in the late nineteenth century and continuing into the early twentieth century. It was built in the imposing 18-size format , making the watch noticeably larger and more substantial than later 16-size and smaller pocket watches. Hamilton Grade 926 Movement The movement is clearly signed: HAMILTON WATCH CO. LANCASTER, PA. 17 JEWELS It is additionally marked: 926 and: ADJUSTED The movement is Hamilton's Grade 926, Model 1 , an 18-size, 17-jewel, manual-wind, lever-set movement made in an open-face configuration. The Grade 926 uses the broad full-plate architecture associated with earlier American watchmaking. Rather than relying on a series of small bridges, much of the movement is covered by large decorated nickel plates. The winding wheels, balance assembly and sections of the gear train remain exposed, giving the movement considerable visual presence. The visible movement retains attractive decorative finishing to the plates along with deeply engraved Hamilton markings. Published specifications for the Grade 926 include: • 18-size construction • 17 jewels • Manual winding

Helen West Heller (1872–1955) was an American painter and master printmaker associated with Chicago’s progressive art movement of the 1920s. A founding voice of the Chicago “No-Jury” Society in 1922, she advocated for independent, non-juried exhibitions that challenged academic tradition. Born in Rushville, Illinois, Heller initially worked in rural isolation before gaining recognition in Chicago and later New York. She became nationally known for her powerful woodcuts, including the celebrated Black Leopards , and for her pioneering 1928 xylographic (woodcut) book Migratory Urge , now considered a collector’s item. After relocating to Brooklyn during the early years of the Great Depression, her work was exhibited at the Brooklyn Museum and acquired by major institutions including the New York Public Library. While highly regarded for her graphic work, Heller considered herself foremost a painter, noted for expressive color, symbolism, and emotionally charged subject matter. Today, Helen West Heller is recognized as an important figure in early 20th-century American modernism and printmaking. Small size: 3 1/2" x 4". Signature: See HWH 32. Condition: Excellent condition. 860047062974.title: Treehouse Painting By Louisiana Folk artist Hank Holland
860047062974.desc: The kids in my hometown would make fun of me because of the way I walked and the way I talked. My speech was slurred, and children could be cruel about things they didn't understand. Daddy saw what I was going through, so he did something that would stay with me for the rest of my life. He built me a treehouse. That treehouse became more than a place to play. It became my refuge—a place where I could climb above the hurt and get away from a world that sometimes made me feel like I didn't belong. It was there that Hank found Hank. Mom added something important, too. She put a big red heart at the base that said LOVE. Years later, that heart would find its way into my paintings. So would the treehouse. And so would the outhouse. People might look at one of my paintings and wonder why there is an outhouse hanging around my beautiful Louisiana trees. To me, it has a much deeper meaning. The outhouse represents the place where you put all the trash in your life—the heartaches, depression, disappointments, rejection, and everything else that causes us pain. You don't have to carry that trash forever. Then there are the people dancing in my paintings. They represent the good times. They remind us to let go, enjoy the life we've been given, and let go and let God. And somewhere in the picture there is faith and hope, because I believe everybody needs somewhere to put their faith and something to give them hope. When people see one of my treehouse paintings, they may see bright colors, Louisiana trees, an old tire swing, a little house and people having a good time. I see my childhood. I see Daddy building a safe place for his little boy. I see Mom's heart telling me I was loved. I see the pain I learned to throw away. And I see the place where a little boy from a small rural town , who was being told by other children that he was different, began discovering who he really was. That's where Hank found Hank. These three paintings would be wonderful to reproduce alongside this chapter because the LOVE heart, treehouse, outhouse, tire swing, dancing figures, church and FAITH imagery allow the reader to actually see your life's symbolism on the canvas.q

Inspired by Louisiana traditions, Hank’s artwork often features Cajun musicians, country churches, fishermen, swamp scenes, celebrations, and everyday Southern life. Every original is created with heart and tells its own story. When you purchase a Hank Holland original, you are receiving an authentic piece of Louisiana folk art directly connected to the artist and the culture that inspires him. Each work is individually made, signed, and truly one of a kind.
